# Auto-generated rule: session-registry-fresh-claim-files-must-be-age-gated

Malformed semantic-id claim files in the session registry can be legitimate in-flight registration state. Zombie sweeps must preserve fresh malformed files and only remove aged ones by filesystem mtime.

## Evidence
Wave 4 reproduced a full-suite race where sweepZombies removed fresh malformed claim files before registerSelf could overwrite them; tests now cover fresh preservation and old malformed removal.

## Extension Review (2026-08-17)

Extended `expires-at` 2026-08-18 → 2026-10-01. TTL for `recurring-issue` is 45 days per
`LEARNING_TYPE_REGISTRY` in `scripts/lib/learnings/schema.mjs`; the date is aligned with the
sibling rule that expired the same day rather than computed to the exact day, so the two
stay reviewable together.

The finding describes a **live** invariant, not a fixed defect — which is why it is extended
rather than deleted. The age-gate is still the mechanism and still load-bearing:
`scripts/lib/session-registry.mjs:318-323` carries it verbatim, comment included —
*"Malformed files can be fresh semantic-session claim files. Use mtime so…"* — and
`age = (now - info.mtimeMs) / 60_000` is what separates `stale-heartbeat` from
`malformed-entry` at line 338. `tests/lib/session-registry.test.mjs:224` pins the behaviour
(*"keeps fresh malformed entries because they may be semantic-id claim files"*).

So the hazard the rule warns about is exactly as reachable today as when it was recorded: a
future edit to `sweepZombies` that treats "malformed" as "delete now" re-opens the race, and
nothing but this rule and that one test says otherwise.
